notes.summary: Visible change for German chats: the failure details the SDK writes itself (tool not permitted, turn limits, endpoint errors, memory tools) show in German. New optional ChatLocale keys activityFailure… and ActivityStep.failures.
notes.howTo: Check tests or CSS that assert the English failure texts in a German chat. An app whose own locale words the activity log keeps English failure texts unless it states language, sets the activityFailure… keys or spreads deChatLocale. A custom activity log can render ActivityStep.failures with stepFailureText(failures, locale, language).

notes.summary: The chat `headers` function and `voice.getToken` may now return a Promise, so a short-lived token or ticket can be fetched per request.
notes.howTo: Drop any cast that forced an async function into `headers` or `getToken`; pass the async function directly.

notes.summary: Chat Markdown lists show bullets and numbers by default, and the new `markdown` prop of AiChatProvider (also VercelAiChat and `<glirastes-chat>`) accepts remark plugins, e.g. for GFM tables.
notes.howTo: Nothing to change. For GFM tables you can run `bun add remark-gfm` and pass `markdown={{ remarkPlugins: [remarkGfm] }}` (memoized) to AiChatProvider. If you added your own list CSS (for example `list-style` overrides) only to get markers, you can remove it.

notes.summary: Completion items set what a pick does with `select`: `chip` (default), `text` (inserts `insertText` or the label as plain text) or `run` (pill, then sends like the send button). `onCompletionSelect` on AiChatProvider can take over a pick.
notes.howTo: Prompt templates that you rewrite from a chip into text in `onBeforeSend` (as omnify does) can return `{ select: 'text', insertText: 'Fasse den Auftrag zusammen' }` from their provider instead; the user sees and edits the text before sending, and the `onBeforeSend` rewrite can go. Return `true` from `onCompletionSelect(item, { trigger, query, controls })` to take over a pick: the typed trigger and query leave the editor and the list closes. For a sub-list, call `controls.openCompletion({ trigger, source: 'templates' })` in `onCompletionSelect` and return `true`; `templates` is a second provider on the same trigger. Nothing changes without these fields.

notes.summary: useChatComposerInput applies initialValue only on mount, as documented. A value that arrives later is ignored; before, the first non-empty value was applied late and reset the caret (typing 'Welche' became 'elcheW W').
notes.howTo: For a draft or prefill that arrives after mount, call the composer's `setText` (or the input handle's `setValue`) instead of relying on a late `initialValue`.

notes.summary: The composer toolbar takes the builtin `plus`: a "+" button with a menu of `attach`, `trigger:<char>` rows, `composer.items` and an optional `source` section of completion entries (`composer.plusMenu`). Without `plus` in the toolbar nothing changes.
notes.howTo: If you built your own "+" or "more" menu next to the composer (via `renderActions` or `components.InputExtra`), put `'plus'` into `composer.toolbar.start` or `end` and list its rows in `composer.plusMenu.items`: `attach` opens the file picker, `'trigger:@'` opens the `@` list with the focus in the editor (named after the trigger's `label`), keys of `composer.items` run their `onSelect(controls)`. `plusMenu.source: { trigger: '/', source: 'templates', label: 'Templates' }` lists that provider's entries directly; choosing one follows its `select` (`text` inserts `insertText`). The menu texts are the optional locale keys `plusMenuButtonLabel` and `plusMenuAttachLabel` (English and German built in).

notes.summary: `AiChatProvider` takes `composer`: `toolbar.start`/`end` order builtin ids (`attach`, `mic`, `actions`, `extra`, `send`, `trigger:<char>`) and your own `items`; `components.ComposerToolbar` lays out the row itself. Without them the composer renders as before.
notes.howTo: If you place the composer's extra buttons through `renderActions` or `components.InputExtra` only to get them into a certain order, list them in `composer={{ toolbar: { start: ['attach'], end: ['mic', 'actions', 'extra', 'send'] } }}` (the default) and move ids around instead. A button that writes `@` into the editor becomes `'trigger:@'`, labeled from the trigger's `label` in `triggers`. Own buttons go into `items` and receive the composer controls in `onSelect(controls)`; `render(controls)` replaces the button. An item key equal to a builtin id replaces the builtin; unknown ids warn once in the console and are skipped. Memoize the `composer` object. `renderActions`, `renderSubmit` and `InputExtra` keep working unchanged. To decide whether an item may write into the composer, read `controls.canCompose` (the editor's own lock; with `queue.enabled` true while a turn streams), not `controls.isLoading`; the `trigger:<char>` buttons and `plus` follow it. `ChatComposerInputControls.canCompose` is a required member, so hand-written mocks or fakes of the controls must add it.

notes.summary: Completion providers may use any single trigger character, e.g. `#` for tickets, not only `@` and `/`. The new provider option `triggers` sets a char's label, pill prefix, default pick behavior and the mention types it owns.
notes.howTo: Set `trigger: '#'` on a `ChatCompletionProvider` to open its list with `#`; add `triggers={[{ char: '#', label, prefix, types: ['ticket'] }]}` (memoized) to AiChatProvider to change the defaults; sent messages, history and `createLocalSessionStore` session titles then show `#` for those types instead of `@` with no further config. Only then the provider calls `session.save(id, messages, { mentionPrefix })` with a third argument; a custom store may use it for its titles or ignore it. When you wrap `createLocalSessionStore`, forward the third argument (`save: (id, messages, options) => base.save!(id, messages, options)`), or its titles lose the prefix. Nothing changes without it: `@` and `/` keep their behavior. `RichMentionInputProps.triggers` widened to `ReadonlyArray<string | ChatTriggerDefinition>` and validates its entries; `composer.inputProps` from `useChatComposerInput` carries `triggers` only when the provider's list differs from the default `@` and `/` (an explicit `triggers` definition or a provider with another char); then spread it before your own `triggers` prop if you set one.

notes.summary: The handler now shows its fixed failure texts in the chat language: a German chat gets `KI-Anfrage fehlgeschlagen` instead of `AI request failed`, and the German text for invalid tool input. Both texts are keys of the handler's `locales` (`streamError`, `invalidToolInput`).
notes.howTo: Nothing to change for a German UI. Tests or log checks that assert on `AI request failed` in a `de*` chat now see the German text. Change the texts per language, or add another language, in the handler's `locales` (`locales: { de: { streamError: '...' }, pl: { streamError: '...', invalidToolInput: '...' } }`; in the runtime container `chat.locales`); languages without a table keep English. The two keys are optional additions to `ChatServerTexts`, so a type built as `Record<keyof ChatServerTexts, string>` or `satisfies Required<ChatServerTexts>` now needs them too. Some texts stay English in a German chat: the permission and budget denials shown by `toolDenialDisplayText`, the unavailable-tool text and the approval-subject refusal texts are not keys of `locales`. The chat UI's activity log still shows these two failures in its own `activityFailureGeneric` / `activityFailureInvalidInput` texts (app overrides included), not the server text: for a text other than the English built-in the stream adds a content-free `data-step-failure` part (`{ toolCallId, code }`) after the call. A test that counts all stream chunks of a German or overridden turn sees that part.

notes.summary: `openCompletion({ trigger, query?, source? })` opens a completion list from code, e.g. a toolbar button: on `useChatComposer()`, `useChatComposerInput()` and the `RichMentionInput` handle. Closing the list untouched removes the inserted trigger again.
notes.howTo: If your toolbar opens the `@` or `/` list by writing the trigger into the editor and dispatching a synthetic `new InputEvent('input')`, call `composer.openCompletion({ trigger: '@' })` from `useChatComposerInput()` (or `useChatComposer().openCompletion`, which waits until the composer is mounted) instead. It does nothing while the composer is locked (`canCompose` false, also on a disabled `RichMentionInput`). It focuses the editor, adds a space when needed, searches at once without the debounce, and `source: 'people'` limits the list to those provider ids (the composer's search and one made by `createCompletionSearch`; an own `onSearch` gets `(query, trigger)` only). Escape, an outside click, blur, an empty result, Enter before the results show (it sends nothing) or an inserted mention remove the text again when the user typed nothing. A custom `RichMentionInputHandle` implementation may add the optional `openCompletion`. `ChatComposerInputControls.openCompletion` and `ChatComposer.openCompletion` are required members, so hand-written mocks or fakes of these types must add them.

notes.summary: createLocalSessionStore accepts maxMessagesPerSession to cap the stored messages per chat. Default is unlimited, so nothing changes unless you set it.
notes.howTo: Pass maxMessagesPerSession (e.g. 120) to createLocalSessionStore instead of trimming messages in your own store. The kept messages start with a user message; the title still comes from the first question.

notes.summary: The voice input's audio worklet path (/audio-worklet-processor.js, unchanged) is now exported as DEFAULT_AUDIO_WORKLET_URL and can be changed with the workletUrl option of the speech adapters, VoiceInputButton and the chat's voice config.
notes.howTo: Nothing to change while the worklet is served at /audio-worklet-processor.js as before. If you serve it elsewhere, you can set voice.workletUrl on the chat or pass workletUrl to the speech adapter; to keep the copy in sync, you can add predev and prebuild scripts that copy node_modules/glirastes/dist/react/audio-worklet-processor.js into public/ (see the speech worklet section of the building-glirastes-chat-ui references).

notes.summary: The Next.js chat handler option `temperature` accepts `null`, which sends no `temperature` to the model (also none to memory summary calls).
notes.howTo: Set `temperature: null` for models that reject it (reasoning models) instead of stripping it from the request. Custom `streamHandler`s still receive `ctx.temperature` as `number | undefined`: `undefined` when the option is `null`, so passing it on to `streamText` keeps compiling.

notes.summary: onTurnEnd(outcome, info) on AiChatProvider (config.onTurnEnd on <glirastes-chat>) is called once when a turn of the open chat ends, with its TurnOutcome and { sessionId }.
notes.howTo: Pass onTurnEnd instead of diffing turnOutcomes to react once per finished, stopped or failed turn. It is not called at an open approval, for stored history, for a chat that is not open or after clear(). Without it nothing changes.

notes.summary: glirastes upgrade report lists release notes since the version this app last reviewed, checked against your code, and is the way agents learn what to do after an upgrade.
notes.howTo: After each glirastes upgrade, or when `glirastes tools refresh` prints its upgrade line, run `glirastes upgrade report` and follow the upgrading-glirastes skill. When the review is done, `glirastes upgrade ack` (with `--defer <id>` for postponed items) records it in `.glirastes/sdk-baseline.json`; commit that file.
